land.text: coastal Andhra around Kandarapura (Chejerla, Guntur district): the Guntur country with Tenali and Ongole named on the Vishnukundina page

successors.note: The Vishnukundina page: "Madhava Varma II took Guntur, Tenali, and Ongole from [the Ananda Gotrikas], probably while they were subordinate to the Pallavas" (no year, c. 440-460). The Ananda Gotrika page says only the dynasty appears to have been "overthrown by the" Salankayanas, which contradicts it.

capitals.name: Kandarapura (Chejerla)
capitals.note: The page: "ruled coastal Andhra with Kandarapura as the capital from 335-425 AD"; the capital was in present-day Chejerla mandal of Guntur district. Coordinates are approximate (the page gives none).

correction.text: coastal Andhra around Kandarapura (Chejerla, Guntur district): the Guntur country with Tenali and Ongole named on the Vishnukundina page

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Ananda Gotrika row. The Ananda Gotrika page gives only "coastal Andhra" and the Guntur district seat; Tenali and Ongole come from the Vishnukundina page and are the researcher's reading of the extent. Cliopatria leaves this land stateless after the Satavahana row, with Late Pallava shapes touching it from 306 and the Gupta shape taking part of it from 347.

region.text: coastal Andhra around Kandarapura (Chejerla, Guntur district): the Guntur country with Tenali and Ongole named on the Vishnukundina page

ledger.note: 335: Kandara founds the Ananda Gotrika kingdom at Kandarapura. "ruled coastal Andhra with Kandarapura as the capital from 335-425 AD"; "Kandara drove [the Pallavas] out of the Amaravati Region" after battles (undated). The land is the researcher's reading.

region.text: coastal Andhra around Kandarapura (Chejerla, Guntur district): the Guntur country with Tenali and Ongole named on the Vishnukundina page

ledger.note: 425: the Ananda Gotrika rule ends. The page's span ends 425 ("flourished from the second half of the 4th century to the first half of the 5th"); it names the conqueror as the Salankayanas, whereas the Vishnukundina page has Madhava Varma II take Guntur, Tenali and Ongole from them in his c. 440-460 reign. The successor is the Vishnukundina page's.

certainty.note: No frontier is given; the extent is the Guntur country with Kandarapura.

sources.title: Ananda Gotrika
sources.note: Period 335-425, the capital Kandarapura (Chejerla), Kandara and the Pallavas, the end (named conqueror).

sources.title: Vishnukundina dynasty
sources.note: Madhava Varma II takes Guntur, Tenali and Ongole from the Ananda Gotrikas.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (named as a counterpart in vishnukundina-dynasty). Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The two pages disagree on the end: 425 and conquest by the Salankayanas (Ananda Gotrika page) against a Vishnukundina conquest in c. 440-460 (Vishnukundina page), a gap of 15-35 years in which the land has no holder. Only three kings are named (Kandara, Attivarman, Damodaravarman) with no reign years. The Pallava relation (subordinate, expelled from Amaravati) is undated. Gazetteer names needed: Kandarapura, Chejerla.
